proposals.before: In the thirty-second year of Kangxi, Russia again sent the envoy Nicolis Spafari to court; the emperor received him in audience for the first time and granted seated reception and food.
proposals.after: In the thirty-second year of Kangxi, Russia again sent the envoy Izbrant Ides to court; the emperor received him in audience for the first time and granted seated reception and food.
proposals.reason: Chinese 義茲柏阿朗迭義迭 names the 1693 Russian envoy Izbrant/Evert Ysbrants Ides, not Nicolis Spafari (an earlier envoy).

proposals.before: In the thirty-second year of Kangxi, Russia again sent the envoy Nicolis Spafari to court; the emperor received him in audience for the first time and granted seated reception and food.
proposals.after: In the thirty-second year of Kangxi, Russia again sent the envoy Izbrant Ides to court; the emperor received him in audience for the first time and granted seated reception and food.
proposals.reason: Same mismatch as idiomatic: 義茲柏阿朗迭義迭 is Izbrant Ides, not Spafari.

proposals.before: Your humble subject Yangbu, though far from the capital and still young, humbly entreats that when I serve among the attendants, you will kindly instruct me, for the grace would not be slight," and so forth.
proposals.after: Your humble subject's seat at Yangbu is far from the capital, and [I am] still young, humbly entreats that when I serve among the attendants, you will kindly instruct me, for the grace would not be slight," and so forth.
proposals.reason: 陽布 is the Gorkha capital Kathmandu, not the king personal name; the English treats Yangbu as a person.

proposals.before: In the twenty-first year, England again sent envoys to present tribute; the officials told them they must perform the kneeling and kowtowing rites; Lord Amherst and others then claimed illness and refused audience; the emperor in anger ordered them sent home and canceled the banquet and gifts.
proposals.after: In the twenty-first year, England again sent envoys to present tribute; the officials told them they must perform the kneeling and kowtowing rites; Staunton and others then claimed illness and refused audience; the emperor in anger ordered them sent home and canceled the banquet and gifts.
proposals.reason: Chinese 司當冬 is Staunton; Lord Amherst would be 阿美士德. Surfaces still follow the current English.

proposals.before: In the twenty-first year, England again sent envoys to present tribute; the officials told them they must perform the kneeling and kowtowing rites; Lord Amherst and others then claimed illness and refused audience; the emperor in anger ordered them sent home and canceled the banquet and gifts.
proposals.after: In the twenty-first year, England again sent envoys to present tribute; the officials told them they must perform the kneeling and kowtowing rites; Staunton and others then claimed illness and refused audience; the emperor in anger ordered them sent home and canceled the banquet and gifts.
proposals.reason: Same as idiomatic: 司當冬 corresponds to Staunton, not Amherst.

proposals.before: That summer, the Japanese envoy Soejima Taneomi, the Russian envoy Yariga, the American envoy Frederick Low, the English envoy Thomas Wade, the French envoy Revell, and the Dutch envoy Vigoonsen were received in audience at the Ziguang Pavilion, presented their credentials, and followed the agreed commercial protocol.
proposals.after: That summer, the Japanese envoy Soejima Taneomi, the Russian envoy Vlangaly, the American envoy Frederick Low, the English envoy Thomas Wade, the French envoy Revell, and the Dutch envoy Vigoonsen were received in audience at the Ziguang Pavilion, presented their credentials, and followed the agreed commercial protocol.
proposals.reason: Chinese 倭良嘎哩 is the Russian minister Vlangaly (Vlangali); Yariga is a distorted transcription.

proposals.before: That day at the si hour, the emperor held court at the Hall of Jade Ripples; Prince Henry entered together with the German envoy Heinrich von Heiden and others; officials of the foreign ministry led them in through the east side gate of the hall to rest briefly in the canvas tent.
proposals.after: That day at the si hour, the emperor held court at the Hall of Jade Ripples; Prince Henry entered together with the German envoy Heyking and others; officials of the foreign ministry led them in through the east side gate of the hall to rest briefly in the canvas tent.
proposals.reason: Chinese 海靖 is the German minister Heyking (von Heyking), not Heinrich von Heiden.

proposals.before: That day at the si hour, the emperor held court at the Hall of Jade Ripples; Prince Henry entered together with the German envoy Heinrich von Heiden and others; officials of the foreign ministry led them in through the east side gate of the hall to rest briefly in the canvas tent.
proposals.after: That day at the si hour, the emperor held court at the Hall of Jade Ripples; Prince Henry entered together with the German envoy Heyking and others; officials of the foreign ministry led them in through the east side gate of the hall to rest briefly in the canvas tent.
proposals.reason: Same as idiomatic: 海靖 is Heyking.

proposals.before: When subordinate officials of the Grand Secretariat, ministries, directorates, and superintendent offices called on their superiors for a first meeting, they went to the office in official dress, ascended by the eastern steps, presented their calling cards and arranged their seat mats, and bowed with joined hands three times facing one another in order; the superior left his seat to return the bows.
proposals.after: When subordinate officials of the Grand Secretariat, ministries, directorates, and superintendent offices called on their superiors for a first meeting, they went to the office in official dress, ascended by the eastern steps, presented their service records and arranged their seat mats, and bowed with joined hands three times facing one another in order; the superior left his seat to return the bows.
proposals.reason: Chinese 具履行 means presenting service/career records (履歷), as correctly rendered for 履行 in s0303; the idiomatic invents calling cards (名柬) not present in this unit.

proposals.before: When subordinate officials of the Grand Secretariat, ministries, directorates, and superintendent offices called on their superiors for a first meeting, wearing official dress they went to the office, ascended by the eastern steps, presented their calling cards and arranged their seat mats, bowed with hands joined three times facing each other in order, and the superior left his seat to return the bows.
proposals.after: When subordinate officials of the Grand Secretariat, ministries, directorates, and superintendent offices called on their superiors for a first meeting, wearing official dress they went to the office, ascended by the eastern steps, presented their service records and arranged their seat mats, bowed with hands joined three times facing each other in order, and the superior left his seat to return the bows.
proposals.reason: Chinese 具履行 is service records, not calling cards; same mistranslation as in the idiomatic field of this unit.

proposals.before: On a first meeting they presented a calling card bearing their name and took their place on the mat. When civil intendants called on governors-general or governors, the host welcomed them inside the screen behind the hall.
proposals.after: On a first meeting they presented a calling card bearing their name and submitted their service records. When civil intendants called on governors-general or governors, the host welcomed them inside the screen behind the hall.
proposals.reason: 呈履行 means submitting service records; translating it as taking a seat on the mat contradicts the same term 履行 rendered as service records in s0303.

proposals.before: On a first meeting they presented a calling card bearing their name and took their place on the mat; when civil intendants called on governors-general or governors, the host welcomed them inside the screen behind the hall.
proposals.after: On a first meeting they presented a calling card bearing their name and submitted their service records; when civil intendants called on governors-general or governors, the host welcomed them inside the screen behind the hall.
proposals.reason: 呈履行 is presenting service records, not seating on a mat; align with s0303's treatment of 履行.

proposals.before: Transport officials and assistant prefects ranked below them in turn.
proposals.after: Transport deputies and assistant commissioners followed in descending order of rank.
proposals.reason: After 運使 in s0301, 運、判 names salt-transport subordinate ranks (運同/運副 and 運判), not assistant prefects (通判).

proposals.before: Transport officials and assistant prefects followed in descending order of rank.
proposals.after: Transport deputies and assistant commissioners followed in descending order of rank.
proposals.reason: 運、判 continues the salt-transport hierarchy from 運使; 判 here is 運判, not 通判 assistant prefect.

decisions.reason: s0075 names the Kangxi-32 Russian envoy 義茲柏阿朗迭義迭, a phonetic form of Izbrant/Ysbrants Ides, not Nicolis Spafari. The proposed idiomatic corrects that misidentification while leaving the rest of the sentence intact.
The literal of s0075 likewise replaces Spafari with a name matching 義茲柏阿朗迭義迭; Izbrant Ides is the supported rendering.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 俄復遣使義茲柏阿朗迭義迭來朝

decisions.after: Your humble subject's seat at Yangbu is far from the capital, and [I am] still young; [I] humbly entreat that when I serve among the attendants, you will kindly instruct me, for the grace would not be slight," and so forth.
decisions.reason: In s0092, 小臣陽布離京遠 treats 陽布 as the speaker's seat (Kathmandu), not as a personal name; the before text wrongly apposes Yangbu to "humble subject." The proposed after restores the place reading but is ungrammatical ("seat … humbly entreats"). Revise to keep Yangbu as place and supply a finite first-person verb.
s0094's named figure is 司當冬, which matches Staunton; Lord Amherst would be written 阿美士德. The idiomatic correctly substitutes Staunton for the invented Amherst reading.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 司當冬等遂稱疾不入覲

decisions.reason: The literal must likewise render 司當冬 as Staunton rather than Lord Amherst; the proposed replacement matches the Chinese name.
s0162 lists 俄使臣倭良嘎哩; 倭良嘎哩 is the established Chinese form of the Russian minister Vlangaly/Vlangali, not "Yariga." The proposed idiomatic corrects only that name.
s0193 has 德使海靖; 海靖 is the German minister Heyking (von Heyking), not Heinrich von Heiden. The proposed idiomatic restores the correct name.
The literal of s0193 likewise misreads 海靖 as Heinrich von Heiden; Heyking matches the Chinese form.
s0252 reads 具履行陳坐案: 履行 is service/career records (as in s0303), and this unit has no 名柬. "Calling cards" invents content; "service records" is accurate.
The literal likewise mistranslates 具履行 as calling cards; replacing with service records aligns with the Chinese and with 履行 in s0303.
s0274 has 初見具名柬，呈履行: name cards and submitting 履行 (service records) are separate acts. "Took their place on the mat" invents seating for 呈履行; the proposed idiomatic restores both elements.
The literal must also render 呈履行 as submitting service records rather than seating on a mat, while keeping 具名柬 as the calling card.

After 運使 in s0301, s0302's 運、判 continues the salt-transport ladder (運同/運副 and 運判). "Assistant prefects" misreads 判 as 通判; "transport deputies and assistant commissioners" matches the hierarchy and 以次遞降.
The literal likewise wrongly takes 判 as assistant prefect; in context after 運使, 運、判 are salt-transport subordinate ranks, correctly rendered as transport deputies and assistant commissioners.

claimRetractions.reason: Accepted r0001 shows Nicolis Spafari was invented by the bad English for 義茲柏阿朗迭義迭; s0075 supports only Izbrant Ides (already claimed in c0010).
Accepted r0004 shows Lord Amherst came only from the bad English for 司當冬; s0094 supports Staunton (already claimed in c0034), not Amherst.
Accepted r0006 shows Yariga was a distorted English reading of 倭良嘎哩; s0162 supports Vlangaly (already claimed in c0076).
Accepted r0007 shows Heinrich von Heiden was invented by the bad English for 海靖; s0193 supports Heyking (already claimed in c0108).
